title: The Lady and Her Five Suitors

keywords: the lady and her five suitors
full_text:
In Baghdad lived an intelligent and virtuous young woman whose husband had been unjustly imprisoned on false charges by an oppressive court. Determined to deliver him, she visited the Chief Justice to petition for his release. The corrupt judge, captivated by her beauty, refused to sign the order unless she granted him a private interview at her house.

Next, she visited the Grand Vizier, then the Chief of Police, then the royal Chamberlain, and finally a wealthy carpenter; all four made the same dishonorable proposition before they would assist her!

Perceiving their corrupt hypocrisy, the clever lady resolved to punish them all simultaneously. She invited each of the five officials to her home on the same evening, at half-hour intervals, and commissioned a large wooden wardrobe with five separate, lockable vertical compartments.

At sunset, the Chief Justice arrived, perfumed and dressed in his finest robes. Just as he sat down, a loud knocking sounded at the gate! The lady cried: 'Alas! My ferocious brother has arrived! Hide in this wardrobe!' The judge scrambled into the first compartment, and she bolted the door.

Next came the Grand Vizier; when the knocking sounded again, he was locked in the second compartment. The Chief of Police was locked in the third; the Chamberlain in the fourth; and the carpenter in the fifth!

With all five corrupt officials safely bolted inside, the lady went directly to the palace of Caliph Harun al-Rashid, requesting an escort of twenty guards to inspect a curious piece of furniture that contained five dangerous pests of the city!

Before the assembled court, the doors of the wardrobe were thrown open: out tumbled the Chief Justice, the Grand Vizier, the Chief of Police, the Chamberlain, and the carpenter, coughing in the dust, red with agonizing shame!

The Caliph laughed until his throne shook, dismissed the corrupt officials from office, released the innocent husband with royal honors, and rewarded the clever lady with a thousand gold dinars for her peerless courage.
moral: Corrupt officials who abuse their authority will find themselves trapped in the ridiculous closet of their own deceit.
